title: Implement verified Multi Color Breathe illumination
description: Derive the complete Multi Color Breathe report layout from immutable SteelSeries GG captures, including ordered colors and applicable zone or connected direction semantics, then add deterministic generation for earcup and supported microphone zones across profiles, CLI, and GTK.
design: Do not generalize the existing single-color Breathe builder until the additional coefficient records and color storage are proven. Use controlled captures for any ambiguous dimensions and require fixture equality before generated hardware writes.
acceptance_criteria: Known GG Multi Color Breathe reports are reproduced byte-for-byte; a new arbitrary supported multicolor sequence and duration are generated deterministically; direction semantics are either physically verified or explicitly constrained; unsupported combinations fail closed; protocol and experiment docs are updated; CLI/profile/GTK round trips are tested; user confirms visible multicolor breathing and successful Steady rollback while audio remains functional.
notes:
GG UI clarification from the hardware owner: Multi Color Breathe accepts up to four selected colors and each selected color fades to black before the next. Existing full-payload microphone frames cover only a one-color case, which is the already generated single-color fade layout.
Existing full-payload capture frames 113 and 131 contain a likely rainbow Multi Color Breathe preset: twelve 8-byte transition records form six positive/negative fade pairs through magenta, blue, cyan, green, yellow, and red, returning to black after each color. The earcups traverse opposite orders. Exact replay and owner observation are required before promoting this inference to verified.
Physical acceptance: generated nine-second red/green/blue Multi Color Breathe on both earcups displayed that order and breathed down to black between colors. This verifies the generalized record chaining for a three-color case. Product input is bounded to the GG manual range of one through four colors; preset parity and fractional speed mapping remain out of scope. Steady rollback succeeded and GameDAC audio devices remained present.
GUI acceptance: owner saved and applied Breathe Test, switched between it and ColorShift, and confirmed fields reloaded correctly. Persisted JSON and status API report multi-color-breathe with its ordered three-color array.
Final integration acceptance: installed binary status API exposed Breathe Test and the enabled Omarchy panel applied it successfully on hardware. Multi-color Sweep now fails closed; legacy single-color Sweep remains supported.
close_reason: Implemented and accepted one-to-four-color Multi Color Breathe across protocol, CLI, profiles, GTK, documentation, generated three-color hardware behavior, rollback, and audio preservation.

title: Implement verified ColorShift illumination
description: Derive the complete ColorShift report layout from immutable SteelSeries GG captures, add deterministic packet generation for earcup and supported microphone zones, expose it through profiles, CLI, and GTK without broadening the HID safety boundary, and physically verify a newly generated color combination on hardware.
design: Treat every byte as observed, inferred, or unknown. Add labeled captures if the existing trace cannot isolate color count, order, duration, or direction. Require fixture equality before the first generated hardware write; preserve Steady rollback and audio.
acceptance_criteria: Known GG ColorShift reports are reproduced byte-for-byte; a new arbitrary supported color sequence and duration are generated deterministically; unsupported combinations fail closed; protocol and experiment docs distinguish evidence from inference; CLI/profile/GTK round trips are tested; user confirms visible ColorShift and successful Steady rollback while audio remains functional.
notes:
GG UI clarification from the hardware owner: ColorShift accepts up to 14 selected colors. The existing full-payload microphone sequence proves only a two-color case and reversed order; complete list cardinality and record chaining must remain fail-closed until controlled multi-color captures establish the layout.
Initial product scope narrowed after correlating the preset capture with reported GG values: expose exactly two ColorShift colors. Although a six-record generated primary-color loop can match frame 37 bytes, the user reports that GG showed a 17.56-second six-marker palette beginning FF9D00 and ending FF00FF, while the packet retained FF0000 and numeric duration 1000. Arbitrary 3-14 color mapping therefore remains unproven.
Physical acceptance: after the VM stopped and usbhid reclaimed interface 0, generated five-second red/blue ColorShift on both earcups visibly passed through purple without fading to black. Steady four-zone rollback succeeded and GameDAC Game remained the default sink.
GUI acceptance: owner saved and applied Shift Test, switched between it and a Multi Color Breathe profile, and confirmed fields reloaded correctly. Persisted JSON and status API report color-shift with its ordered two-color array.
Final integration acceptance: installed binary status API exposed Shift Test and the enabled Omarchy panel applied it successfully on hardware.
close_reason: Implemented and accepted two-color ColorShift across protocol, CLI, profiles, GTK, documentation, fixture equality, physical hardware behavior, rollback, and audio preservation.

title: Choose public project name and branding
description:
## Decision
Select the public repository, binary, application display name, and compatibility subtitle before GitHub publication. The decision is pending user acceptance; current recommendation is gamedacctl.

## Rationale
gamedacctl is immediately discoverable to Linux users, follows a familiar ctl naming convention, currently has no GitHub search collision, and appears less vendor-official than steelseries-gamedac-linux.

## Alternatives Considered
GlowDAC is a more neutral and polished brand but is less searchable and may be mistaken for an audio-DAC project. LumenDAC has the same ambiguity. Retaining steelseries-gamedac-linux is explicit locally but visually resembles a vendor-owned repository and is unnecessarily long for a binary name.
design: Prefer gamedacctl because it is discoverable, Unix-native, currently absent from GitHub search, and the ctl suffix reduces official-product ambiguity. Do not rename the local checkout or create a GitHub repository until the user accepts the name.
acceptance_criteria: Name is checked in the intended GitHub namespace, receives a basic package/web/trademark collision review, uses original artwork, and is documented with an independent-project compatibility disclaimer.
close_reason: Accepted gamedacctl for repository, package, binary, and future app; public namespace and crates.io collision checks passed; explicit unofficial compatibility disclaimer added; no artwork currently shipped.

title: Resolve animated header and generate Breathe packets
description: Determine the role of animated header RGB offsets 2-4, reproduce known Breathe packets from structured inputs, then verify one new color and duration plus connected Sweep, Synchronized, and reverse behavior.
design: Follow every exact-capture, exact-generation, new-combination, and product-promotion gate in docs/research-process.md.
acceptance_criteria: Generated known cases match captures byte-for-byte; one new case is physically verified with static rollback; unknown Reflected or ColorShift semantics remain fail-closed.
close_reason: Generated Breathe/Sweep reports match eight GG fixtures byte-for-byte; new Synchronized and Sweep cases physically verified with static rollback; reverse flag reproduced with visual-direction ambiguity documented; unsupported effects remain fail-closed.

title: Replace root execution with scoped device access
description: Provide a narrow, reviewable udev-based access path for GameDAC 1038:1280 interface 0 so the CLI and GUI never invoke sudo or require a privileged daemon.
design: Prefer TAG+=uaccess or an equivalently narrow supported mechanism. Do not grant broad hidraw access.
acceptance_criteria: An active desktop user can control only the intended HID interface without root; reconnect works; audio device 1038:1282 remains available; permission removal has a documented rollback.
notes: Installed the exact source-controlled udev rule and verified live scope: only 1038:1280 interface 00 receives uaccess and the active-user ACL; interfaces 01/02 and 1038:1282 interface 05 remain excluded. Rule-removal plus logical reconnect removed access and caused gamedacctl to fail closed with Permission denied. Reinstall plus logical reconnect restored access automatically. A final manual upstream-cable disconnect/reconnect produced full remove/add events for both products; interface 00 regained access, non-root four-zone static control succeeded, the default six-channel sink returned at 60 percent, and the user heard spoken audio. Note: even a control-only authorization cycle briefly resets the audio sibling.
close_reason: Scoped non-root access, exclusion boundaries, fail-closed removal rollback, logical reconnect, manual cable reconnect, controller recovery, and GameDAC audio recovery were all verified.

title: Implement safe controller core and CLI
description: Create a typed packet and transport boundary for verified static earcup and microphone controls, off, exact captured presets, validation, and dry-run output without claiming unsupported effects.
design: Keep packet builders pure and transport separate. Retain the Python research utility as executable reference during migration.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture tests cover every byte and zone mask; malformed and unsupported inputs fail closed; verified commands preserve GameDAC audio and have physical acceptance evidence.
notes: Implemented native Rust packet/core/CLI boundary with static earcup and microphone zones, explicit off targets, guarded exact-pcap replay, HID interface selection, dry-run output, 12 passing tests, strict clippy, and documentation. Added exact SHA-256 regression checks for known Sweep, Synchronized, and five-second Breathe reports. Pending: install scoped udev rule, physically verify Rust static/mic/off/replay writes, reconnect behavior, and unchanged 1038:1282 audio before closure.
close_reason: Implemented and physically accepted the non-root Rust controller core: deterministic packet fixtures, fail-closed validation, independent earcup and microphone colors, every off target, exact Synchronized replay, and preserved GameDAC 5.1 audio.

title: Build native GameDAC Linux controller
description: Deliver the standalone Linux lighting controller and optional Omarchy integration defined in docs/app-plan.md while preserving Linux audio and the documented safety boundary.
design: docs/app-plan.md is the canonical architecture and milestone specification. docs/research-process.md governs protocol promotion. docs/legal.md governs publication boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: All child work required for the chosen release scope is complete; supported behavior is physically verified; packaging and publication safeguards are satisfied.
close_reason: Initial product scope complete: supported behavior was physically accepted, desktop and Omarchy UX shipped, permissions/storage/packaging hardened, and v0.1.3 published through the guarded workflow and destination-verified. Three optional hardware-research items remain explicitly deferred and do not block this milestone.

Add repository metadata, visual proof, concise cross-links, and structured issue intake; do not claim unsupported hardware or GG/audio parity.

Both repositories cross-link clearly and expose their distinct responsibilities. Documentation validation and each repository's relevant checks pass.

Omarchy README now requires gamedacctl 0.1.3, leads with installation and scope, routes issues by responsibility, and includes a clean 380x272 live panel screenshot. 2026-09-05 correction: the concurrent source and README edits were intentional terminology work from another terminal, not unrelated work. Reconciled them into this task. The public CLI now displays --target effect while accepting the previous --target earcups spelling as a hidden alias; a regression test proves identical output. Fresh GUI render and screenshot visually confirm the new labels. Full validation passes with 25 library and 15 CLI tests.

Controller hosted run 33991662360 passed full validation, clean-room Arch bundle inspection, checksum verification, and dry-run upload. Omarchy plugin validation passed locally. title: Automate release publication with GitHub Actions
description: Replace the manually executed gamedacctl release process with a repository-owned GitHub Actions workflow. The v0.1.0 process manually validated both repositories, created a filtered Cargo source archive, generated and tested an Arch package, assembled checksums and release notes, pushed a tag, published a prerelease, downloaded every asset, and verified the published checksums. Future releases should make that sequence repeatable and reviewable.
design: Use a tag-driven or manually dispatched workflow that creates a draft or prerelease first. Verify that the tag, Cargo package version, Arch pkgver, and plugin compatibility metadata agree before publishing. Run scripts/validate, create a source artifact that excludes raw USB captures and internal agent/task metadata, build and test the x86_64 Arch package in a pinned Arch environment with Cargo locked/frozen, generate PKGBUILD/SRCINFO and SHA256SUMS from the actual artifacts, inspect package contents, and verify downloaded release assets. Resolve the current source-archive/PKGBUILD checksum cycle with a generated release recipe or checksum-substituted template. Grant contents:write only to the release job, never to pull_request code; pin third-party actions by commit SHA; do not expose signing credentials unless a separately reviewed signing design is adopted. Decide whether the Omarchy plugin needs its own lightweight tag/release workflow or only validation on controller releases.
acceptance_criteria: A documented dry run builds the same release asset set without publishing; a controlled test tag produces a draft or prerelease containing the Arch package, filtered source archive, PKGBUILD, SRCINFO, SHA256SUMS, and release notes; versions and checksums are derived rather than manually copied; full project and package tests pass; raw captures and repository-internal metadata are absent from the source artifact; package metadata and file contents are checked; a destination-side download verifies every published checksum; workflow permissions are least-privilege and actions are SHA-pinned; failure before final publication leaves no misleading stable release; the manual fallback and rollback procedure are documented.
notes: Implemented and documented .github/workflows/release.yml, scripts/build-release, and generated Arch recipe flow. Main dry runs: 33973034633 (v0.1.0, success after rustup dependency fix), 33973293978 (v0.1.1, success), 33973840807 (corrected v0.1.2, success). Tag runs: 33973498480 published v0.1.1, whose independent public download exposed nested docs/AGENTS.md in the source archive; retained immutable release and hardened the builder to reject AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md at any depth. Run 33974051731 published corrected v0.1.2 successfully. Independent public verification confirmed tag v0.1.2 resolves to e3cecc3cdd48752e773e878d8ff8125ee95f0bdc; release is non-draft prerelease; all five expected assets exist; SHA256SUMS verifies source, package, PKGBUILD, and SRCINFO; package metadata and paths are correct; source archive contains no agent instructions, raw captures, Beads, Claude, or Codex metadata. Local scripts/validate and full local package build also passed. Manual fallback and rollback are in docs/release-process.md; Omarchy plugin remains source-only and outside this compiled release workflow.
close_reason: Automated release pipeline proven by corrected v0.1.2 publication and independent destination verification.

title: Harden XDG profile storage
description: Audit and harden saved-profile persistence while preserving the existing $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/gamedacctl/profiles.json location (default ~/.config/gamedacctl/profiles.json) and schema. The current location correctly follows XDG_CONFIG_HOME, but writes use a predictable .tmp name, permissions inherit the caller umask, the parent directory is not synced after rename, and concurrent GUI/CLI writers can overwrite newer state.
design: Keep lighting profiles and their user preferences in XDG_CONFIG_HOME because they are application configuration. Preserve version-1 files and the current path with no destructive migration. Use a unique temporary file in the same directory, restrictive user-only creation permissions, file sync followed by atomic rename and parent-directory sync, and a defined cross-process serialization strategy for GUI and CLI updates. A malformed store must produce an actionable error and must not be silently replaced. Package removal must leave user profiles untouched.
acceptance_criteria: Existing profiles load without migration or value changes; XDG_CONFIG_HOME overrides and the default ~/.config path are tested; new directories/files have intentional permissions; interrupted writes cannot replace the last valid store; concurrent CLI and GUI operations cannot silently lose profiles or the selected-profile state; malformed JSON remains recoverable and is never automatically overwritten; storage location, backup, and uninstall behavior are documented; full validation passes.
notes: 2026-09-05 implementation complete: preserved the version-1 XDG path and schema; all mutations now serialize through a private advisory lock and reload current disk state, then use a unique same-directory 0600 temporary file, file sync, atomic persist, and directory sync. The GUI no longer mutates its in-memory store before persistence succeeds and malformed initial data is surfaced without replacement. Added permissions, rejected-update, malformed-data, concurrent profile, concurrent selection/policy, default-path, and legacy coverage. Full scripts/validate passes with 23 library and 12 CLI tests. A read-only run against the owner actual four-profile store returned ready and preserved SHA-256 a4d4db2b35a5f28cd561f939c3508346304f32f609341176ba217bb72f80c0bd, mode 0644, and size 1035 exactly; its mode will become 0600 on the next successful write.
close_reason: XDG profile storage is compatibility-preserving, private on write, serialized across writers, durable through synchronized atomic replacement, corruption-safe, documented, and fully validated.

title: Add per-profile icons
description: Allow each saved lighting profile to carry an optional user-chosen emoji or glyph, expose it through the stable status JSON, and render it in the Omarchy profile selector with the existing effect icon as fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Existing profile files remain compatible; the GTK editor can save and reload an optional bounded icon; status JSON exposes the icon; the Omarchy panel renders it and still falls back safely; tests and both repository validators pass.
close_reason: Optional bounded profile icons are backward compatible, editable and persistent in GTK, exposed through status JSON, rendered with safe fallbacks in Omarchy, refreshed live through an event-driven file watcher, and human-verified by changing to a pasted rainbow icon.

title: Derive reconnect readiness from passive HID input
description: Replace or shorten the conservative four-second reconnect delay only if unsolicited 64-byte input reports from GameDAC control interface 0 can be correlated with lighting-engine readiness. The HID descriptor exposes 64-byte input, 64-byte output, and 1024-byte feature reports; existing captures contain repeated device-to-host 0x10 reports and later 0x20 reports, but their semantics across enumeration are unknown.
design: Read unsolicited HID input passively through the known interface; do not invent a polling command. Keep the GUI responsive, bound all waits, retain a four-second fallback, distinguish kernel write completion from physical application, and verify audio recovery after each manual upstream reconnect.
acceptance_criteria: A labeled reconnect capture records enumeration, uaccess timing, first 64-byte HID input reports, attempted profile writes, and physical two-earcup results across repeated trials. A readiness predicate is implemented only if it predicts successful complete writes reliably; otherwise the tested fixed-delay fallback remains. No unknown output, feature, or firmware query is sent.
notes:
2026-09-05 preliminary passive trials: a settled three-second observation opened the control node but received zero 64-byte input reports. A complete 60-second manual upstream reconnect observation recorded input read failure at 19.392s, device absent at 19.647s, and /dev/hidraw15 accessible again at 35.176s; zero unsolicited input reports arrived before removal or after access returned. Existing capture 0x10/0x20 input records therefore are not a dependable heartbeat based on current evidence. Keep the physically accepted four-second post-access fallback; do not send an unobserved GET_REPORT or other query. A repeatable raw reconnect capture is still required before closing.
2026-09-05 deferred after v0.1.3: passive observation found no dependable unsolicited readiness report, while the bounded four-second post-access fallback was physically accepted with lighting and audio recovery. Resume only with new repeatable reconnect evidence; do not invent firmware polling.

title: Verify connected direction with distinct colors
description: Capture and physically compare normal and reversed connected effects using distinct per-zone or multicolor values so direction is visually distinguishable. Use a marked static start state, hold duration and all other fields constant, compare complete reports byte-for-byte, and document whether Engine's reverse flag changes visible direction. Keep multicolor generation fail-closed until accepted.
design: Follow docs/research-process.md. Prefer colors with clearly different hue and luminance, repeat each direction from the same static marker, and preserve the original captures immutably.
acceptance_criteria: A labeled full-payload capture contains normal and reversed distinct-color cases; packet differences are documented; the user can distinguish or explicitly cannot distinguish physical direction under a controlled replay; any generated multicolor support remains blocked on exact fixture equality and rollback.
notes: 2026-09-05 deferred after v0.1.3: supported effects are physically accepted and the reverse flag remains conservatively represented; resume only if distinct-color direction semantics become a user need or new capture evidence is available.

title: Prepare legally cautious public release
description: Choose original branding and an open-source license, document compatibility and experimental boundaries, produce reproducible Arch packaging, and review all distributed material against docs/legal.md.
design: Use SteelSeries marks only descriptively. Generated protocol code, not GG components or captured packets, must power release binaries.
acceptance_criteria: Release includes independent-project disclaimer, compatibility matrix, original assets, no proprietary files or raw whole-bus captures, reviewed udev access, and legal review before any commercial distribution.
notes:
2026-09-05 audit before pause: both public repositories lack LICENSE files; the plugin README still describes publication as future and needs an explicit independent-project/non-affiliation disclaimer; reproducible Arch packaging remains incomplete. Raw captures were checked as device-filtered to 1038:1280 with no obvious credentials or device serials. Paused to complete the advertised illumination effect set first.
2026-09-05 release-hardening pass: added a precise compatibility/support matrix and README boundary; added Cargo repository/readme/keywords/categories metadata and excluded raw captures plus project-agent/task metadata from Cargo source packaging; added plugin non-affiliation disclaimer and corrected its published install wording. Full controller validation (31 tests plus docs, udev, desktop, fmt, clippy) and plugin validation pass. Remaining gate: owner must choose an OSS license before LICENSE files, Cargo license metadata, and the Arch package recipe can be finalized and tested. Recommended default: MIT OR Apache-2.0.
2026-09-05 completed: selected MIT OR Apache-2.0 in both repositories; published controller prerelease v0.1.0 with direct Arch package, checksum-pinned filtered Cargo source archive, PKGBUILD, SRCINFO, and SHA256SUMS. The package was built twice via makepkg from the release archive; the final build passed 26 distributable tests, package metadata/content inspection, extracted CLI dry-run, desktop validation, udev validation, and shared-library resolution. GitHub destination verification downloaded every asset and all four SHA-256 entries passed. Package SHA-256: cdfa143b776d7ed88b8309bdc5f08fa97a3e808fe1470de05c71e3e9696f610c. Source SHA-256: b2a911f3f6f36c399cbbe310b7373c7fd893e47f5a38fa60faf4e42c2eb5ee1e. Release: https://github.com/AndreasDellrud/gamedacctl/releases/tag/v0.1.0
2026-09-05 post-release acceptance: the owner downloaded and installed the published Arch package and reported that it worked.
close_reason: Public prerelease v0.1.0 is licensed, compatibility-scoped, packaged for direct Arch installation, and destination-verified.

title: Add thin Omarchy shell adapter
description: Provide an optional Omarchy bar widget and panel for device status and profile selection without placing USB, packet, polling, or privilege logic inside omarchy-shell.
design: Distribute as a separate manifest-root plugin repository after the native controller interface is stable.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin manifest validates; enable, reload, and removal work; controller failure cannot destabilize omarchy-shell; the plugin communicates only through the stable native API.
close_reason: Thin Omarchy adapter accepted: stable native JSON boundary, separate manifest-root plugin, validated lifecycle and contained failure behavior, successful real profile apply, and human-confirmed visual interactions.

comments.author: Andreas Dellrud
comments.text: Implemented the stable native boundary (, ) with CLI coverage and created the separate manifest-root project at ~/Projects/omarchy-gamedacctl. Omarchy 4.0.1 manifest validation, add, enable, open, source reload, disable, removal, and re-add all succeeded. comments.author: Andreas Dellrud

title: Build native desktop UI and profiles
description: Build a portable Linux GUI and profile model over the stable controller core with explicit device, permission, disconnected, and write-result states.
design: Prefer GTK4/libadwaita for the native UI and add D-Bus only when front-end serialization or reconnect persistence requires it.
acceptance_criteria: No root prompt; profile persistence survives restart; reconnect policy is opt-in; all exposed controls map only to verified core features; Linux audio is unchanged.
close_reason: Native GTK4/libadwaita UI and atomic versioned profile store implemented on current Rust/GTK bindings; profile restart persistence and opt-in path-aware delayed reconnect restore physically verified on both earcups; audio returned and GameDAC 5.1 remained default; dedicated UX and passive-readiness research retained as follow-ups.

title: Perform dedicated desktop UX and visual design pass
description: Refine the functional GTK/libadwaita desktop controller after the interaction model stabilizes. Improve information hierarchy, color selection, profile management, responsive sizing, accessibility, empty/error states, and original visual identity without copying SteelSeries GG artwork or trade dress.
design: Keep protocol and transport logic in the shared Rust library. Use current GTK4/libadwaita components and preserve the verified effect boundary. Treat the present window as a functional prototype, not the final visual design.
acceptance_criteria: The UI is reviewed at narrow and normal window sizes; colors use an accessible picker plus exact hex entry; keyboard and screen-reader labels are present; profile create/update/delete flows and empty/error states are clear; original artwork and styling follow docs/legal.md; user accepts the resulting UX.

title: Select among multiple connected GameDACs
description:
## Problem
The controller currently selects the first matching 1038:1280 interface 0. That is convenient for the normal single-device case but ambiguous if more than one identical original GameDAC is connected.

## Scope
Enumerate matching compatible devices, preserve zero-configuration behavior when exactly one exists, and provide an explicit CLI/application selector when multiple matches exist. Refuse all writes while selection is ambiguous.
design: Use verified VID/PID/interface/report characteristics as the compatibility boundary. Prefer a device serial as the durable selector when exposed; otherwise present a clearly labeled physical/sysfs path with documented reconnect limitations. Never guess or silently choose the first device when multiple compatible units are present.
acceptance_criteria: One matching GameDAC continues to work without a selector; zero devices reports not found; multiple matches list distinguishable choices and fail closed until one is selected; tests cover enumeration and selection without hardware; the selected transport cannot open a different match; GUI/profile implications are documented.
notes: 2026-09-05 deferred after v0.1.3: the normal single-GameDAC path is safe and verified; selector work should resume when there is a real multi-device hardware/use case to validate identity and UX against.
